answer: Churn is counted in ridge, and dawn publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 9% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. Anyone who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the relic history. Every extra alias adds 12 hours of verification and 29 percent more locked value. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
